clue.text: As a tense scene from a Peter Pan production would do, if a harness broke?

definitions.text: As a tense scene from a Peter Pan production would do, if a harness broke?

parts.words: As a tense scene from a Peter Pan production would do, if a harness broke?
parts.note: the flying actors in a stage Peter Pan hang on wires, so a snapped harness drops them literally downwards, and the dramatic scene becomes a comic shambles

explanation.surface: A stagehand imagines the nightmare of a wire failing mid-flight in a Peter Pan show.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: actors would literally drop down on to the stage, and the serious scene would collapse into slapstick comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink into ridiculous chaos is the idiomatic meaning, here acted out literally by a falling performer.

clue.text: Swinging instrumentalist, a corrupt, hag-ridden Trojan

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or debased, telling us to break up and rearrange the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A tormented, depraved Trojan is somehow described as a swinging musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges HAGRIDDEN and TROJAN; the 'a' is only a link. Swinging refers to swing jazz, not a pendulum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian-born gipsy guitarist was a leading figure of swing jazz in 1930s Paris.

clue.text: Country star hiding short, coarse hairstyle

indicators.note: the star word hides the hairstyle by holding it within itself

parts.note: the Sun is our nearest star
DA is the short form of duck's arse, a crude name for a 1950s swept-back haircut

explanation.surface: A country music star conceals a crude haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country star' reads as a singer, but the definition is just 'Country'. DA, duck's arse, is a 1950s quiff swept back at the sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The African nation south of Egypt is a country, which is all the definition asks.

clue.text: Previously more of a noble character?

definitions.meaning: a jokey comparative of earl, meaning more like a nobleman of that rank

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of early means previously, and a playful comparative of the peer's title fits the second reading.

clue.text: Make meaningful call in small office

indicators.note: the call word sits inside the office word

parts.note: DEPT is the abbreviation for department, a section or office
to cry is to call out

explanation.surface: Someone makes a significant phone call from a tiny office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make meaningful call' reads as one phrase; split it after 'meaningful'.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a cipher turns gibberish into a readable message, making it meaningful.

clue.text: Spike column: "Digital End Smoother"

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike
a file is a line of people or things one behind another, like a column

explanation.surface: A newspaper spike column runs a headline about a smoothing gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means relating to fingers here, not computers: the device smooths the ends of the digits.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery board or metal file shapes and smooths fingertips, the ends of the digits.

clue.text: A gallery for ever indebted for works that are?

definitions.text: A gallery for ever indebted for works that are?

parts.words: A gallery for ever indebted for works that are?
parts.note: a museum keeps borrowed artworks indefinitely, so it is perpetually in debt to the lender for them; the question mark invites the playful reading

explanation.surface: A gallery is perpetually grateful for certain pieces in its collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The museum phrase is read as owing for ever: works lent indefinitely leave the gallery permanently indebted.
explanation.definitionFit: Artworks lent indefinitely by an owner to a museum are described with this phrase.

clue.text: Brief, bound (made by squirrel?)

parts.note: a flying visit is a brief one
a bound is a jump

explanation.surface: A short jump, perhaps performed by a squirrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hints at the flying squirrel, which glides from tree to tree in a great jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A running jump is something a flying squirrel might naturally be imagined making.

clue.text: Solar system model's alternative second attempt (temperature dropped)

parts.note: OR introduces an alternative

indicators.note: the temperature letter is let fall from the attempt word

parts.note: a retry is a second attempt

explanation.surface: A model of the planets gets a second go after the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: '(temperature dropped)' removes T from RETRY to leave RERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A clockwork model of the planets circling the Sun is named after an Earl of Cork and Orrery.

clue.text: Bank, say, welcoming one legendary character who tragically went under

definitions.text: legendary character who tragically went under

indicators.note: the lender takes in the word for one

parts.note: a bank is an example of a lender
A means one

explanation.surface: A riverbank receives a mythical figure who drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a riverbank to fit the drowning, but it is the financial kind. 'welcoming' puts A inside LENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth swam the Hellespont nightly to Hero and drowned one stormy night.

clue.text: Topiarist's craft?

parts.note: craft suggests the skill of a hedge-shaper, but it means a boat, punning on the cutting tool such a gardener uses

explanation.surface: A question about the skill of someone who sculpts hedges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' means a vessel: the fast sailing ship shares its name with the hedge-cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast nineteenth-century sailing ship shares its name with the shears used to trim hedges.

clue.text: One untying knots without electronic skill

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the anagram wraps round the letter
knots means tangles, so the letters of untying are jumbled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A person unpicking knots without any electronic aid shows skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: 'knots' jumbles UNTYING to NGNUITY, which then goes round E, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleverness or inventiveness is a kind of skill in devising things.

clue.text: See 1 across
Toupee back to front on university teacher

indicators.note: the hairpiece word is turned round

parts.note: rug is slang for a toupee

explanation.surface: A university teacher wears his toupee the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' turns the slang word round; 'on' just places it before the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritual mentor in Hindu tradition, and by extension any revered teacher.

clue.text: Plant cash container in religious building

indicators.note: the cash container sits inside the building word

parts.note: a friary is a house of friars
a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: Someone plants a cash box inside a religious building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb meaning hide, but it is the definition, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake's head is a bulbous flowering plant of the lily family with chequered bells.

clue.text: Major, say, once grabbing padding of her bust in town

indicators.note: the prime minister letters clutch the middle letter

parts.note: John Major was formerly PM, prime minister

indicators.note: padding is the stuffing in the middle, so take the centre letter of her

parts.note: bust means broke, penniless

explanation.surface: A former prime minister grabs at a woman's padded bra in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her bust' is not one idea: 'padding of' takes E from 'her', and 'bust' alone is BROKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in south-west Wales with a medieval castle, birthplace of Henry VII.

clue.text: River's colour: it's pasty

parts.note: the Rhine is a major European river, plus the possessive s
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A river's hue is described as pale and unhealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like pallid, but means made of paste, the glass used for imitation gems.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation diamond made of paste glass is a pasty thing in the literal sense.

clue.text: Stand for special event to give something extra in performance

parts.note: to rise is to stand up
to here means for, as in a toast to someone
an occasion is a special event

explanation.surface: Someone stands up at a ceremony to deliver an outstanding performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand for' reads as tolerate, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to respond to a challenge by performing better than usual.

clue.text: Much of which contributes to jam trade

definitions.text: Much of which contributes to jam
definitions.meaning: cars and lorries on a road pile up into a jam, not fruit preserve
to deal or barter, often in illicit goods

explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles clog roads into jams, and the verb means to deal commercially, especially illegally.

clue.text: Lead present in unusual spell of rain — it's blissful

indicators.note: the lead word is found inside the jumbled rain
the letters of rain are spelt in an unusual order

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army, short for vanguard

explanation.surface: Lead appears in a strange spell of rain, which is apparently delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell of rain' suggests a shower, but 'unusual spell of' jumbles the four letters to NIRA, and 'present in' puts the lead word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddhist state of perfect peace, freed from desire, is a blissful condition.

clue.text: See 7
Over 3 years of light travel makes you break down with cold

parts.note: to parse a sentence is to break it down grammatically
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A long journey of light makes someone collapse with a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break down' reads as collapse, but means grammatical analysis.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomical unit is about 3.26 light-years, the distance light covers in over three years.

clue.text: Hermaphrodite is in possession of inverted form of address

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so in a horizontal light the run is read backwards

parts.note: bi, short for bisexual, loosely stands for having both natures
has means possesses

explanation.surface: A double-sexed creature somehow owns a polite title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' turns the whole run BIHAS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A respectful title for a man in colonial India, equivalent to sir.

clue.text: Scientific instrument switches are remote

indicators.note: switches means swaps around, telling us to rearrange the following letters

explanation.surface: Switches on a scientific device turn out to be remote controls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' looks like a noun for controls, but rearranges ARE REMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for measuring the density or weight of air or gases.

clue.text: Religious leader's state day included in greeting

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts

indicators.note: the day letter goes inside the greeting

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A religious leader's statement includes a day in a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition stands for 'is', a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam, the guided one expected to appear before the end of the world; also a title of leaders.

clue.text: Don't keep going on about "Fort Fun"!

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to stop banging on about some amusement park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is the anagram signal for FORT FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch something off is to stop it running; it is also a bore, apt to someone going on.

clue.text: Single-handedly circumnavigating the unending "heart of Ireland"

indicators.note: sailing round, so the solo word goes round the other piece

parts.note: doing something alone is doing it single-handedly

indicators.note: unending means without its end, so the last letter of the is dropped

explanation.surface: A solo sailor circles round the heart of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims 'the' to two letters; 'circumnavigating' fits the solo-sailing surface while placing them inside the solo word.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Shannon in County Westmeath, near the geographical centre of Ireland.

clue.text: See 16 down
